title: Lipschitz-Constrained EEGNet: Improving Robustness Against Adversarial Perturbations in BCI
summary: This paper proposes Lipschitz-Constrained EEGNet, a modified EEGNet architecture with Parseval-tight frame constraints on convolutional layers to limit Lipschitz constants, improving robustness against adversarial examples in EEG-based BCIs. The approach combines EEGNet's compact structure with Parseval network principles, validated through adversarial attack detection rates and CLEVER score comparisons against standard EEGNet and FBCSP baselines.
gap: Existing EEGNet models lack formal robustness guarantees against adversarial perturbations, which is critical for safety-critical BCI applications.
approach: Introduce Parseval-tight frame constraints on EEGNet's convolutional layers to bound Lipschitz constants, ensuring small input perturbations do not disproportionately affect outputs. Use semidefinite programming for constraint enforcement during training.
evaluation: Compare adversarial detection rates (AUC scores) against white-box attacks (FGSM, PGD) and CLEVER scores for robustness quantification. Baselines include standard EEGNet and FBCSP. Test on P300, ERN, and SMR paradigms from MOABB datasets.
